body: Yes, for reason it gets terminated before this runs. This is where we need @cescoffier 's expert knowledge to help out :)

I think there is more to it than that. When the test is stopped a sequence of shutdown tasks are executed, on of which leads to KafkaConsumer being closed (if you go higher up the callstack you'll see that this is down to smallrye-reactive-messaging observing a shutdown event).
When the mailer is not there, the shutdown works just fine

When it fails, the value of `state` is defined to `ST_TERMINATED` in `SingleThreadEventExecutor`. In this case the method `isShutdown` returns `true`.
I guess the mailer call the `cleanup();` method in `doStartThread` because it is only in the `finally` block that the `state` is defined to `ST_TERMINATED`.
However, hard to debug :(

I have seen this sort of problem a lot. Generally the solution is to catch RejectedExcecutionException and if it is due to shutdown either just run the task directly, or start a new thread to run the shutdown task.

@stuartwdouglas It's too bad that `runOnContext` doesn't indicate at all whether or not an exception was thrown (and I am assuming that changing this core Vert.x class it is out of the question in the short term).
The only way I see around the problem is to change the shutdown code of the Kafka client to use a new thread instead of the Context.

issue.body:
This is meant to avoid cases where the Context had already been shutdown.
See: https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/4834.

Basically what was observed is that in a Quarkus application that contains Kafka Client and Mailer, the Kafka Client could not shutdown properly because  `io.vertx.core.impl.ContextImpl#runOnContext`
was throwing a `java.util.concurrent.RejectedExecutionException`  with a message saying that event executor has been terminated.
